title: Background Catalogue
description: The real, complete SF2E background catalogue (154 entries), extracted live from gamesystems/sf2e/packs/backgrounds for the induction terminal's Page 3 (design/induction-terminal.md). Singleton file: data/campaign/background-catalogue.json.

boosts.description: One entry per boost slot (almost always 2; one real background, Escaped Experiment, has 3). Same shape and resolution rule as ancestry-catalogue.json's boosts -- a single-ability entry is fixed, a multi-ability entry is a free choice among exactly those abilities; core/boost-slots.mjs resolves a player's pick against this shape.

trainedSkills.description: Fixed (non-Lore) skill(s) this background trains, informational only -- NOT a player choice the terminal resolves. Some real backgrounds offer a prose CHOICE the flat data doesn't capture (e.g. Starship Dweller: 'trained in the Crafting or Piloting skill'); the `description` field is always the source of truth for those cases. Empty array is real and means the raw compendium data didn't capture a skill grant this cleanly -- check `description`.

loreSkills.description: Named Lore skill(s) this background trains, informational only, same caveat as trainedSkills. A background listing two Lore names occasionally means 'choose one of these' rather than 'grants both' -- check `description`.

feat.description: The background (skill) feat this background grants, by name, informational only -- deliberately NOT resolved/picked here, same reasoning as ancestry feat and class feats/spells (design doc §5): it's a real menu pick with its own rule text, deferred to the real character sheet post-induction. Null for the few real backgrounds that grant no feat at all.

description.description: Real Player Core / setting-book flavor text, HTML-stripped, @UUID inline-links resolved to their label text. Includes the background's own mechanical sentences verbatim (unlike ancestry-catalogue.json's pure-flavor description) -- background prose routinely embeds the exact boost/skill/feat wording, and is the only place a genuine choice (e.g. 'Crafting or Piloting') is preserved.
